header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Redwood Product), Nate Zhao (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (NoviHealth Head of ML), Jonas Reed (NoviHealth Platform Eng), Liam O'Hare (NoviHealth CTO), Sophie Tran (NoviHealth SRE)
summary: High-level sandbox onboarding to compare INT8 vs FP8 precision profiles across NoviHealth's conversational triage workload. Discussed latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), quality metrics (BLEU/QA checks + custom evals), fallback rules to FP16, KV caching behavior, and security requirements (VPC peering, KMS). Agreed next steps for sandbox access and benchmark artifacts.
topics:
1) Intro & goals
2) Target latency & quality KPIs
3) Quantization profiles: int8 vs fp8 tradeoffs
4) Sandbox walkthrough + metrics to collect
5) Security/ops constraints (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
6) Rollout & fallback plan
7) Next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samira, account exec on the Redwood Optimize team. Quick round-robin?
[00:08] Maya Patel: Maya here, head of ML at NoviHealth. We're excited to dig into the quant stuff, we've been trying to shave latency on the triage flow.
[00:15] Diego Rivera: Diego, solutions engineer. I'll do the sandbox setup and the perf bits.
[00:20] Jonas Reed: Jonas, infra. I'll worry about VPC peering and onboarding.
[00:25] Liam O'Hare: Liam, CTO. We care about cost too — want to see the delta per-1000 reqs.
[00:30] Samira Khan: Great. Goal for today: run through the precision playbook for INT8 vs FP8, show the console sandbox flow, explain the fallback story and what observability we'll give you. Also confirm your SLOs.
[00:45] Maya Patel: Our target is roughly p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms for single-turn triage prompts. p99 ideally < 900ms but we can relax if quality drops.
[00:55] Diego Rivera: Good, that gives us a nice band. Quick note — some of the numbers assume continuous batching. For triage, you might run small batches so we can tune the batching window on our runtime.
[01:05] Sophie Tran: We run spikes in the morning, so burst capacity matters. How does dedicated vs hosted play here?
[01:15] Samira Khan: For predictable p99 we'd usually recommend Dedicated if you need guaranteed tail latency, but the sandbox will show what hosted with smart routing and cache gets you.
[01:25] Diego Rivera: Okay jumping into the demo — opening the Optimize console, sandbox cluster "novi-sbx-1". We're going to spin three profiles: int8-aggressive, fp8-balanced, and fp16-fallback.
[01:40] [screen share noise — short pause]
[02:10] Diego Rivera: The console shows per-profile token latency distributions, and quality overlays driven by your eval set. Note, the eval hooks currently sample 2% by default — we can bump that.
[02:30] Jonas Reed: Quick question — what's the KV cache behavior across precision variants? We worry about cold starts and cache compatibility.
[02:40] Nate Zhao: Good one. The KV cache format is compatible across precision on our runtime; key/value semantics are preserved. There may be minor warmup differences but you won't lose your cached prefixes when switching between int8 and fp8.
[02:55] Maya Patel: I've seen 'KV cash' get misheard in transcriptions before, ha.
[03:00] Samira Khan: Ha, yeah our transcript does that too. Back to tradeoffs — INT8 tends to give the most cost savings, but FP8 tends to preserve quality for longer sequences, especially for hallucination-sensitive prompts.
[03:20] Maya Patel: Any rule-of-thumb for where to put the cutoff? Sequence length / task type?
[03:28] Diego Rivera: We usually look at your eval metrics: if QA F1 drops more than 1.5% versus FP16 at the int8 profile then it's a red flag. For triage classification with short prompts, int8 often passes. But for long-note summarization sections, FP8 or FP16 might be safer.
[03:48] Liam O'Hare: What's the delta on p50/p95 if we move from fp16 to fp8 or to int8 — numbers ballpark?
[03:56] Diego Rivera: Ballpark on A100-like instances: FP16 -> p50 ~ 80ms, FP8 -> ~70ms, INT8 -> ~58ms for same model and small tokens. p95 and p99 improvements depend on batching and routing policies. Int8 can shave 20–30% CPU/GPU time often.
[04:20] Maya Patel: We're using a Llama-derivative model with a 4k context; will int8 still be safe?
[04:28] Diego Rivera: For Llama-family 4k, int8 is pretty mature, but you want to run a sensitivity sweep. We'll run that in the sandbox. Also run your prompts through our quant-sensitivity harness from the console.
[04:40] [15s pause as Diego changes tabs]
[04:55] Diego Rivera: Demo: configuring a sweep. Select dataset (you can upload later), choose sample size — suggest 500 examples from your triage logs — and pick metrics (BLEU, QA F1, hallucination score).
[05:10] Jonas Reed: About data residency and logs — do we have options for retention and redaction?
[05:18] Samira Khan: Yes, in Dedicated/Private you get full control over retention. Hosted has configurable retention windows and redaction rules; audit logs are available and we integrate with your SIEM via forwarders.
[05:30] Sophie Tran: KMS? We can't have keys in vendor-managed KMS.
[05:35] Nate Zhao: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) and HSM integration in Private deployments. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions — we can go over specifics in the security doc.
[05:50] Maya Patel: Good. For the sandbox, will logs include prompts? We need to scrub PHI.
[05:58] Samira Khan: Sandbox defaults to redacted transcripts. You can provide a scrub list or use our PII redaction rules; we'll only store hashes if you ask. We'll include config details in the folder we share.
[06:10] Diego Rivera: Now, hands on: I'm starting a run comparing int8-aggressive vs fp8-balanced. You'll see the dashboard populate. Note that throughput on the int8 profile is higher and cost-per-token lower.
[06:30] [dashboard updates]
[06:45] Diego Rivera: Look at quality overlay — at sample id 127, int8 dropped answer relevance by 3 points vs fp8. That's flagged. The console links back to the sample transcript and the token-level attention heatmap.
[07:05] Maya Patel: That token-level view looks helpful. Can we hook that into our internal eval labels?
[07:12] Priya Menon: Yes, we can map your label schema via the eval connectors; Diego will add the mapping.
[07:20] Liam O'Hare: If we decide to roll int8 to 50% traffic, what's the rollback strategy?
[07:26] Diego Rivera: Canary via traffic split + automatic rollback on quality regression threshold. You can configure thresholds per metric. We also have a fallback lane that routes failing requests to fp16 or your pinned model.
[07:40] Jonas Reed: What about cold starts when fallback triggers? That could spike p99.
[07:45] Nate Zhao: We mitigate via warm standbys and pre-warming on spikes. Also smart routing prefers nearby instances to avoid cross-region latencies.
[07:56] Maya Patel: Can we control batch windows tight enough to keep p50 low?
[08:02] Diego Rivera: Yes, you can tune batching window and max batch size. For triage with low latency you want short windows and smaller batches. Our autoscaler can then add more nodes for throughput.
[08:20] Samira Khan: Quick architecture note — the runtime uses quant-aware kernels and momentary reordering to maximize occupancy. Sometimes this shows up as non-linear gains with FP8 depending on the kernels available on a given GPU.
[08:36] Liam O'Hare: Any hardware lock-in? If we choose GPUs with certain tensor cores, does behavior change?
[08:42] Diego Rivera: Performance varies by GPU generation; we surface a model-to-hardware profile in the console. We'll include recommended instance types for your workload in the benchmark sheet.
[08:55] [10s pause]
[09:10] Jonas Reed: About permissions: RBAC for who can flip profiles in production?
[09:15] Priya Menon: Console supports role-based access controls and audit trails. You can lock deploy controls to a small team.
[09:24] Sophie Tran: We need SSO with SAML and SCIM sync.
[09:28] Samira Khan: Supported. We'll include the SSO setup checklist in the follow-up.
[09:36] Diego Rivera: Back to the sandbox — I'm kicking off a stress run with your sample set. It will run int8 -> fp8 -> fp16 fallback for any example that fails the quality threshold. The run should take ~30 minutes.
[09:50] Maya Patel: Great. While that's running, can we talk cost modeling? We need a per-1M token ballpark with int8 vs fp8 vs fp16.
[09:59] Samira Khan: We'll send the pricing matrix but ballpark: int8 ~ 40–55% of fp16 cost, fp8 ~ 65–80% depending on utilization and sequence length. These are rough numbers; sandbox numbers will be more precise.
[10:20] Liam O'Hare: What about hybrid profiles — like int8 for short prompts, fp8 for long ones automatically?
[10:26] Diego Rivera: Yep. You can configure routing rules in Optimize: if sequence length > 1k tokens route to fp8, else int8. You can also split by prompt type or user segment.
[10:38] Maya Patel: Do we get observability per user segment?
[10:41] Nate Zhao: Yes, console supports per-route and per-customer-segment dashboards and can emit traces to your tracing backend.
[10:48] Jonas Reed: For the sandbox run, what artifacts will we get back?
[10:52] Diego Rivera: Full run artifacts: per-sample diffs, token-level deltas, latency histograms, cost estimates, and a recommended precision profile per route. We will drop them into a shared folder and link from the console.
[11:05] [pause — Diego typing]
[11:20] Diego Rivera: The run completed. Initial quick look: int8 passed 92% of your triage examples within the 1.5% QA F1 tolerance. FP8 passed 98%. The console has flagged the failing 8% with examples.
[11:35] Maya Patel: That's interesting. Can we see those 8% and annotate which are safety/PHI concerns?
[11:42] Diego Rivera: Absolutely — the flagged list includes sample ids and transcripts. You can annotate them and re-run the sensitivity test.
[11:50] Sophie Tran: Any weird outliers?
[11:52] Nate Zhao: There's a cluster around very long patient notes where int8 hallucinated more frequently — likely due to attention kernel differences. FP8 had marginally better behavior.
[12:05] Samira Khan: Sounds like a candidate for hybrid — int8 for short triage requests, fp8 for long-note processing, and fp16 fallback for flagged prompts.
[12:15] Liam O'Hare: Sounds reasonable. From a rollout standpoint, we'd prefer a staged approach: sandbox -> canary 10% -> 50% -> full. We'd like auto-rollback on QA drop >1.5%.
[12:29] Samira Khan: That matches our recommended playbook. We'll provide an example rollout policy in the shared folder.
[12:35] Jonas Reed: On security checklist — SOC 2, ISO27001, SAML, KMS, audit logs. We'll need an attestation.
[12:42] Samira Khan: We'll attach our security pack (SOC2 + SOC2 Type II details, penetration test summary) to the folder. Also a technical contact for the private deployment path if you want on-prem.
[12:55] Maya Patel: If we go dedicated, how long to provision?
[12:58] Diego Rivera: Depends on capacity but usually 2–6 weeks for dedicated pods; private on-prem longer. We can discuss timeline in the procurement thread.
[13:10] Liam O'Hare: Who signs the SLA?
[13:13] Samira Khan: We'll route to enterprise contracts; you can expect standard SLAs with uptime and latency targets for Dedicated if you pick that path.
[13:25] Diego Rivera: Quick demo note — the console's rollouts page shows active canaries, percent traffic, metric windows, and rollback history. You can attach your custom eval metrics there too.
[13:40] Maya Patel: Let's capture a simple acceptance criterion: int8 must not drop QA F1 by more than 1.5% and p99 must remain under 1s for production traffic. If both hold at 50% traffic, we'll expand.
[13:55] Samira Khan: Noted — we'll put that in the runbook.
[14:05] Jonas Reed: Any items to flag on networking? VPC peering, private link?
[14:10] Nate Zhao: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink. For Private deployments we also support air-gapped setups. We'll share network diagrams.
[14:22] Sophie Tran: Great. A couple of nitty-gritty questions — does the fallback impose double billing when routed to two models?
[14:29] Diego Rivera: No, fallback only charges for the model that actually served. If you route to a standby and it returns, we charge for that exec. We can configure early-exit on failing heuristics to avoid double processing.
[14:45] Maya Patel: Can the console surface cost-per-call at the route level?
[14:49] Priya Menon: Yes, cost breakdown per token, per route, per model version. We'll include sample graphs.
[14:58] Liam O'Hare: Ok, timecheck — we've got 10 minutes left. Any open blockers?
[15:02] Maya Patel: Sandbox access and the sample prompt upload — we need the sandbox link and creds.
[15:06] Diego Rivera: I'll provision and email creds.
[15:09] Jonas Reed: We'll also need the security pack and SSO checklist.
[15:12] Samira Khan: We'll attach both.
[15:15] Maya Patel: Last question — can we schedule a deeper SRE-level session on autoscaling behavior?
[15:19] Nate Zhao: Yes, we should do a 60-minute SRE deep dive next week. I'll propose slots.
[15:25] Samira Khan: Perfect. Recap of action items and who does what coming up in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[15:33] Liam O'Hare: Thanks all.
[15:36] [meeting ends]
closing_recap: Recap: Sandbox run completed with initial results — int8 passed ~92% of triage examples within tolerance, fp8 98%. Agreed playbook: hybrid routing by sequence length, rollout canary with auto-rollback threshold 1.5% QA F1. Deliverables: security pack, pricing matrix, sandbox creds, and benchmark artifacts. Next meetings: SRE deep dive (60m) and technical deep dive week of 2027-04-19.
